passages.text: Hear the word of the LORD, O children of Israel, for the LORD has a case against the people of the land: “There is no truth, no loving devotion, and no knowledge of God in the land!
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people of Israel.
The LORD commands the children of Israel to listen to His word.
The LORD has a case against the people who live in the land.
There is no truth in the land.
There is no loving devotion in the land.
There is no knowledge of God in the land.
passages.original: שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֣י רִ֤יב לַֽיהוָה֙ עִם־ יוֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֠י אֵין־ אֱמֶ֧ת וְֽאֵין־ חֶ֛סֶד וְאֵֽין־ דַּ֥עַת אֱלֹהִ֖ים בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Cursing and lying, murder and stealing, and adultery are rampant; one act of bloodshed follows another.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel commit many sins.
They curse.
They lie.
They murder.
They steal.
They commit adultery.
These sins are everywhere.
Bloodshed follows bloodshed.
One violent act leads to another.
passages.original: אָלֹ֣ה וְכַחֵ֔שׁ וְרָצֹ֥חַ וְגָנֹ֖ב וְנָאֹ֑ף פָּרָ֕צוּ וְדָמִ֥ים בְּדָמִ֖ים נָגָֽעוּ׃

passages.text: Therefore the land mourns, and all who dwell in it will waste away with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air; even the fish of the sea disappear.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God says the land mourns.
Everyone who lives in the land wastes away.
The animals in the fields waste away.
The birds in the sky waste away.
Even the fish in the sea disappear.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֣ן׀ תֶּאֱבַ֣ל הָאָ֗רֶץ וְאֻמְלַל֙ כָּל־ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בָּ֔הּ בְּחַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה וּבְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְגַם־ דְּגֵ֥י הַיָּ֖ם יֵאָסֵֽפוּ׃

passages.text: But let no man contend; let no man offer reproof; for your people are like those who contend with a priest.
passages.sermon:
Do not let anyone argue.
Do not let anyone correct another.
Your people act like those who argue with a priest.
Your people resist authority.
Your people refuse correction.
Your people challenge those who should guide them.
passages.original: אַ֥ךְ אִ֛ישׁ אַל־ יָרֵ֖ב וְאַל־ יוֹכַ֣ח אִ֑ישׁ וְעַמְּךָ֖ כִּמְרִיבֵ֥י כֹהֵֽן׃

passages.text: You will stumble by day, and the prophet will stumble with you by night; so I will destroy your mother— My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I will also reject you as My priests. Since you have forgotten the law of your God, I will also forget your children.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
You will stumble during the day.
The prophet will stumble with you at night.
I will destroy your mother.
My people are destroyed because they lack knowledge.
You have rejected knowledge.
I will reject you as My priests.
You have forgotten the law of your God.
I will forget your children.
passages.original: וְכָשַׁלְתָּ֣ הַיּ֔וֹם וְכָשַׁ֧ל גַּם־ נָבִ֛יא עִמְּךָ֖ לָ֑יְלָה וְדָמִ֖יתִי אִמֶּֽךָ׃ נִדְמ֥וּ עַמִּ֖י מִבְּלִ֣י הַדָּ֑עַת כִּֽי־ אַתָּ֞ה הַדַּ֣עַת מָאַ֗סְתָּ וְאֶמְאָֽסְאךָ֙ מִכַּהֵ֣ן לִ֔י וַתִּשְׁכַּח֙ תּוֹרַ֣ת אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֶשְׁכַּ֥ח בָּנֶ֖יךָ גַּם־ אָֽנִי׃

passages.text: The more they multiplied, the more they sinned against Me; they exchanged their Glory for a thing of disgrace.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His people.
His people increased in number.
As they increased, they sinned more against God.
They turned away from God.
They gave up their honor.
They chose shame instead of glory.
passages.original: כְּרֻבָּ֖ם כֵּ֣ן חָֽטְאוּ־ לִ֑י כְּבוֹדָ֖ם בְּקָל֥וֹן אָמִֽיר׃

passages.text: They feed on the sins of My people and set their hearts on iniquity.
passages.sermon:
The priests feed on the sins of My people.
The priests desire wrongdoing.
The priests set their hearts on evil.
The priests seek out iniquity.
passages.original: חַטַּ֥את עַמִּ֖י יֹאכֵ֑לוּ וְאֶל־ עֲוֺנָ֖ם יִשְׂא֥וּ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: And it shall be like people, like priest. I will punish both of them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
The people and the priests are alike.
Both people and priests do wrong.
God will punish both for their actions.
God will repay both for what they have done.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֥ה כָעָ֖ם כַּכֹּהֵ֑ן וּפָקַדְתִּ֤י עָלָיו֙ דְּרָכָ֔יו וּמַעֲלָלָ֖יו אָשִׁ֥יב לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: They will eat but not be satisfied; they will be promiscuous but not multiply. For they have stopped obeying the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The people have stopped obeying the LORD.
They will eat.
They will not be satisfied.
They will be promiscuous.
They will not multiply.
passages.original: וְאָֽכְלוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׂבָּ֔עוּ הִזְנ֖וּ וְלֹ֣א יִפְרֹ֑צוּ כִּֽי־ אֶת־ יְהוָ֥ה עָזְב֖וּ לִשְׁמֹֽר׃

passages.text: Promiscuity, wine, and new wine take away understanding.
passages.sermon:
Promiscuity confuses people.
Wine confuses people.
New wine confuses people.
These things take away understanding.
People lose good judgment because of them.

passages.text: My people consult their wooden idols, and their divining rods inform them. For a spirit of prostitution leads them astray and they have played the harlot against their God.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel turn to wooden idols for advice.
They ask their divining rods for answers.
A spirit of prostitution leads them away from the truth.
They are unfaithful to their God.
passages.original: עַמִּי֙ בְּעֵצ֣וֹ יִשְׁאָ֔ל וּמַקְל֖וֹ יַגִּ֣יד ל֑וֹ כִּ֣י ר֤וּחַ זְנוּנִים֙ הִתְעָ֔ה וַיִּזְנ֖וּ מִתַּ֥חַת אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: They sacrifice on the mountaintops and burn offerings on the hills, under oak, poplar, and terebinth, because their shade is pleasant. And so your daughters turn to prostitution and your daughters-in-law to adultery.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel worship idols.
They offer sacrifices on the tops of mountains.
They burn incense on the hills.
They do this under oak trees, poplar trees, and terebinth trees.
They choose these places because the shade is pleasant.
Because of this idol worship, your daughters become prostitutes.
Your daughters-in-law commit adultery.
passages.original: עַל־ רָאשֵׁ֨י הֶהָרִ֜ים יְזַבֵּ֗חוּ וְעַל־ הַגְּבָעוֹת֙ יְקַטֵּ֔רוּ תַּ֣חַת אַלּ֧וֹן וְלִבְנֶ֛ה וְאֵלָ֖ה כִּ֣י ט֣וֹב צִלָּ֑הּ עַל־ כֵּ֗ן תִּזְנֶ֙ינָה֙ בְּנ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם וְכַלּוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם תְּנָאַֽפְנָה׃

passages.text: I will not punish your daughters when they prostitute themselves, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery. For the men themselves go off with prostitutes and offer sacrifices with shrine prostitutes. So a people without understanding will come to ruin.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God says, “I will not punish your daughters when they become prostitutes.
I will not punish your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery.
The men themselves go with prostitutes.
The men offer sacrifices with shrine prostitutes.
The people do not understand.
A people without understanding will be ruined.”
passages.original: לֹֽא־ אֶפְק֨וֹד עַל־ בְּנוֹתֵיכֶ֜ם כִּ֣י תִזְנֶ֗ינָה וְעַל־ כַּלּֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ כִּ֣י תְנָאַ֔פְנָה כִּי־ הֵם֙ עִם־ הַזֹּנ֣וֹת יְפָרֵ֔דוּ וְעִם־ הַקְּדֵשׁ֖וֹת יְזַבֵּ֑חוּ וְעָ֥ם לֹֽא־ יָבִ֖ין יִלָּבֵֽט׃

passages.text: Though you prostitute yourself, O Israel, may Judah avoid such guilt! Do not journey to Gilgal, do not go up to Beth-aven, and do not swear on oath, ‘As surely as the LORD lives!’
passages.sermon:
Israel turns away from God.
Israel acts like a prostitute.
Judah must not become guilty like Israel.
Do not go to Gilgal.
Do not go up to Beth-aven.
Do not make oaths saying, “As surely as the LORD lives.”
passages.original: אִם־ זֹנֶ֤ה אַתָּה֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַל־ יֶאְשַׁ֖ם יְהוּדָ֑ה וְאַל־ תָּבֹ֣אוּ הַגִּלְגָּ֗ל וְאַֽל־ תַּעֲלוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית אָ֔וֶן וְאַל־ תִּשָּׁבְע֖וּ חַי־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: For Israel is as obstinate as a stubborn heifer. Can the LORD now shepherd them like lambs in an open meadow?
passages.sermon:
Israel acts stubbornly.
Israel is like a heifer that refuses to obey.
The LORD cannot guide Israel.
The LORD cannot lead them gently.
The LORD cannot care for them like lambs in a wide, open field.
passages.original: כִּ֚י כְּפָרָ֣ה סֹֽרֵרָ֔ה סָרַ֖ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עַתָּה֙ יִרְעֵ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה כְּכֶ֖בֶשׂ בַּמֶּרְחָֽב׃

passages.text: Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone!
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
Ephraim worships idols.
Ephraim is closely connected to these idols.
Do not interfere with Ephraim.
Leave Ephraim alone.

passages.text: When their liquor is gone, they turn to prostitution; their rulers dearly love disgrace.
passages.sermon:
The people finish their drinking.
They turn to prostitution.
Their rulers love shame.
Their leaders seek disgrace.
passages.original: סָ֖ר סָבְאָ֑ם הַזְנֵ֣ה הִזְנ֔וּ אָהֲב֥וּ הֵב֛וּ קָל֖וֹן מָגִנֶּֽיהָ׃

passages.text: The whirlwind has wrapped them in its wings, and their sacrifices will bring them shame.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Israel and Ephraim.
God says a whirlwind surrounds them.
The whirlwind holds them tightly in its wings.
Their sacrifices will not help them.
Their sacrifices will bring them shame.
passages.original: צָרַ֥ר ר֛וּחַ אוֹתָ֖הּ בִּכְנָפֶ֑יהָ וְיֵבֹ֖שׁוּ מִזִּבְחוֹתָֽםס
